title: Kobi <> Cedrick - Wagertech Deal and CMS Integration Walkthrough

items.topic: Existing prerequisite Jira story stays valid
items.statement: Kobi said the Jira story Cedrick already completed is fine because it was a prerequisite; the remaining deal life cycle / CMS stories in Jira will change based on the final design.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the stories that are in Jira right now, um, the one that you already did, I think that's fine, uh, because that was a prerequisite anyways. / Kobi Kunasekaran: but for the rest of them, I think um I think based off of the uh the design conversations and um the final design that I've kind of uh worked together on um some of those are going to change. So, I will get those updated.

items.topic: Update existing Jira stories to final design
items.statement: Kobi will update the existing Jira stories that change because of the final deal life cycle / CMS integration design.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: some of those are going to change. So, I will get those updated.

items.topic: Epic scope: CMS integration plus deal life cycle
items.statement: The epic covers two things: the CMS integration and its prerequisite, the deal life cycle. This phase of the CMS integration syncs deals and affiliate links to the CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, for for the scope of this epic, it's actually two things. One is a CMS integration. Um, but the prerequisite for the CMS integration is a deal life cycle. Um, because the whole point of the CMS integration, at least the phase of the CMS integration is syncing the deals and affiliate link uh over to the CMS, right?

items.topic: Deal creation via screen flow, not New button
items.statement: Deal creation moves away from the standard New button to a screen flow that holds the deal makeup fields.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they're using the standard new button um to create the deals. Um, except I want to move away from this. So, we are going to do a screen flow um that uh it's mostly packed out um that they're going to use instead to create a new deal.

items.topic: Deal makeup fields define deal uniqueness
items.statement: The deal makeup fields are operator, partner, market country, market state, vertical and source; together they make a deal unique. Kobi corrected himself that it is more than five fields.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Operator, partner, market country, market state, vertical, and source. I guess it's not five fields, it's more than five, but those are the deal makeup fields for a deal. That's what makes a deal unique.

items.topic: New default status 'New' for deals
items.statement: A new deal status 'New' will be introduced as the default status for every newly created deal; a Jira ticket will cover it because the status does not exist yet.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: when we create a deal through the screen flow um we're going to introduce a new status called new. Um this is going to be the default status that every new newly created deal gets created as. Um there's going to be a jur ticket for this. Um because we don't have the new status right now in place.

items.topic: Status changes only via controlled actions
items.statement: Users must not edit deal status directly; all life cycle moves (new to activated, activated to paused, retired, etc.) go through controlled action buttons, not standard record page edits. Kobi called this a constraint across the board.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I want them to update the life cycle of the deal through controlled uh actions. So whether to move from a new to activated uh activated to paused uh retired, whatever it is, we're going to make sure that they're all done through uh action buttons as opposed to standard record page edits. / Kobi Kunasekaran: but in at no point should they be able to just freely edit the status page directly. I think that's just like a constraint that we want to make across the board.

items.topic: Lock deal ID fields read-only, incl. admins
items.statement: Deal ID fields that are user-editable today, even for admins, will be locked so users see a read-only version. Kobi said this is in the stories.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: even like the deal ids and stuff like that um in a lot of areas right now it's user editable uh e even for admins and I want to make sure that uh those fields are locked down so they see just like a readonly version um and not an editable version out of the standard ones. Again, this is something that is in the stories.

items.topic: Commercial terms section in creation screen flow
items.statement: Commercial terms fields on the deal will be their own section in the creation screen flow; the user can add them during deal creation or skip and add them later through a screen flow. Kobi said this design is not finished yet.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: there I'm thinking about an additional section for commercial terms uh which is a another design that I'm working on um that I will I still need to finish and add in um but we decided that on deals right now there's this there's a bunch of fields called commercial terms that uh is going to be its own section uh in that screen flow for the user to either choose to add it during dual creation or they can skip it and add it later on through a screen

items.topic: Commercial terms as bolt-on after deal creation
items.statement: Cedrick should not focus on commercial terms for now; Kobi will treat it as a bolt-on after the new deal creation logic is in place.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: but for now, don't worry too much about commercial terms. I'm going to treat it as like a bolt-on after we have the new deal creation logic.

items.topic: Pre-activation edits recompute keys with dup check
items.statement: Until a deal is activated, users can change any makeup field. On change, the deal external ID, deal name and makeup key must update, and validation must still flag when another deal with the same makeup already exists. Nothing goes to the CMS before activation.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: until the deal is activated, we're going to allow the users to change anything that's here. … When they do those things, we need to make sure that um we are updating the deal external ID, the deal name, and the makeup key to match whatever the latest update is. … we need to make sure that the validation still pops up to say if another deal already exists with that same makeup. / Kobi Kunasekaran: until the deal is activated nothing happens to the CMS.

items.topic: Must affiliate links exist before activation?
items.statement: Whether users must add affiliate links before activating a deal is to be clarified with the client. For now Kobi assumed at least one link is needed before the deal can be pushed to the CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I I want to say that they need to do it before they activate the deal, but that's a EBD to clarify with them. Um, but for now, let's just say that at least we need at least one link before we can push it to CMS.

items.topic: Activation pre-check gate before CMS sync
items.statement: Clicking the activate button runs a final validation that the deal has everything needed for the CMS. If the pre-check fails, the deal does not move to Activated. This is a second gate after the minimum-required-fields validation at creation.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: When they click on the button to activate the deal, I want to uh trigger a validation. Uh one more final validation to check for uh anything that we may need to ensure that the deal is uh deal has everything we need to send it to CMS. / Kobi Kunasekaran: If the day if that pre-check fails, then the deal should not move to the activated status. Okay. So, that's like a second gate.

items.topic: Status date fields and first/last activation
items.statement: Kobi proposed a date field per status, set every time the deal enters that status, plus first and last activation dates.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: basically like for each of the statuses um I'm proposing we create a uh date field to track … every time it goes into the respective statuses um and then for activation I want to track the first time a deal is activated and last time a deal is activated

items.topic: Lock makeup fields after activation for all
items.statement: Once a deal is activated, nobody (ops, management or admins) can edit the core makeup fields in the UI.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, once the deal is activated, nobody should be able to edit any of those uh any of those makeup fields. Um whether it's ops, management, uh admins. … but in terms of the UI, um once a deal is activated, it's locked down.

items.topic: Post-activation makeup edits stay manual
items.statement: Editing makeup fields after activation is a separate manual workflow with no automation now. Kobi is drafting a manual admin override process (for example through Inspector, with some validations).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm drafting a separate like manual override adminedit process where they may be able to do it through like inspector or something like that still with some validations. / Kobi Kunasekaran: if they need to edit any of the makeup fields or anything like that, that's a whole other manual workflow. We're not doing any automations for that right now. Um so we're going to keep that as a manual process once the deal is activated.

items.topic: Activation triggers first CMS sync
items.statement: Deal activation is the starting point for the first CMS sync: build the payload, send it, capture and save the response, and handle the result. Kobi did not yet know the exact trigger mechanism.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: basically the deal activation is the starting point for the first sync to CMS. Uh you know put together the payload, sync it to CMS, capture the response and save uh save the response and handle it depending on what happened uh when you sent that request over.

items.topic: Non-critical fields stay editable post-activation
items.statement: After activation, fields not sent to the CMS stay editable, for example redeposit required, commercial terms and notes. Makeup fields and other mission-critical fields stay locked. Kobi said the list may evolve.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: There are going to be other fields like redeposit required for example is not uh is not a dependency for the CMS. … the fields that they can't edit are things like the operator partner like the makeup fields and anything else that's mission critical.

items.topic: Are effective start/end dates sent to CMS?
items.statement: Kobi was unsure whether effective start and end dates are sent to the CMS; he said it is TBD.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: effective start end date. Uh actually I think these we are sending um this is TBD

items.topic: Post-activation status changes trigger CMS sync
items.statement: Only fields in the CMS payload should trigger a re-sync. Every post-activation status change (paused, inactive, closed, review required, retired), including the automated inactive moves, triggers a CMS sync with the latest deal makeup.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: essentially only the fields that are part of the payload that we're sending to CMS should trigger another sync. … they could move it to paused, inactive, closed, review acquired, retired. All of these should trigger a CMS sync with the latest makeup of the deal information. / Kobi Kunasekaran: every status change gets synced to CMS.
items.critic_note: Field-change part is hedged: Kobi said 'I don't know if I got to that part of the design yet' before 'only the fields that are part of the payload ... should trigger another sync'; later (line 498) he said status and affiliate link changes are the only resync triggers. Status-change sync is firm; field-level resync triggers remain unconfirmed.

items.topic: Auto inactive / reactivate based on signups
items.statement: Similar to the player automation, a deal moves to Inactive if it has no signup records for a defined period, but only when its current status is Active. A counterpart moves an Inactive deal back to Active when a signup comes in. The time period was not defined.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Inactive, we're going to add similar automation to what you did for I think it was player where if there's no signup records for an x amount of time, uh then we move a deal to inactive but only if the pre the current status is active. … And then we would need a counterpart to that um where if a deal is inactive but a signup comes in then we move that to active.

items.topic: Simple screen flows per status change
items.statement: Kobi suggested simple gated screen flows for each status (for example pause, close), with a reason field if the client needs one, and possible validations per status.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So what I'm thinking is just simple screen flows, right? And if there are uh specific requirements like if they need a reason to capture for pause, we'll include that in the screen flow. / Kobi Kunasekaran: There may be some validation and prerequisites to check for each one.

items.topic: Retired status releases deal makeup key
items.statement: Because the CMS cannot delete a deal, a Retired status is used. Retiring is the only time the makeup key changes: '-R' plus the Salesforce deal ID is appended, which releases the makeup so a new deal with the same makeup can be created. Cedrick agreed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So to get around that, that's where we have the retired status. And I scoped this out as well. So when a deal is retired, um this is the only time where we update the deal makeup key / Kobi Kunasekaran: whatever the current deal makeup key is, once the deal is retired, we'll just add the Salesforce deal ID and a dash r to indicate that it's retired. This way it releases a deal makeup key / Cedrick Infantado: Yeah, makes sense.

items.topic: CMS keys on deal external ID, not makeup
items.statement: Kobi recalled from the last meeting that the CMS side will not enforce unique deal makeup and will operate on the deal external ID; a retired deal keeps its external ID, so changes upsert into the existing CMS record.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: also talked about in the in the last meeting where stra was in uh we said that they he's like they're not going to do any enforcement of unique deal makeup. Um, they're just going to make sure that like we we're we're going to operate with the deal external ID specifically. So, as long as we keep the same deal ID on this retired deal, um, any changes to that deal is just going to upsert into uh the existing record.

items.topic: Makeup key internal-only; external ID increments
items.statement: The deal makeup key is internal, unique, used for deduplication and not sent in the API payload. Kobi believes the deal external ID formula is already built to append an increment (e.g. 001) so a new deal with a reused makeup gets a unique external ID; the retired deal's external ID stays the same.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The deal external ID formula I believe it's already built to add like a 001 at the end so that it's always going to be unique. / Kobi Kunasekaran: so the deal makeup ID is not something we send through the uh API. This is internal only. Uh and we use this uh to dduplicate deal creation. / Cedrick Infantado: I thought that's the external ID. So for the external ID it would remain the same and for the new one that / Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct.
items.critic_note: Statement softened: Kobi said 'I believe it's already built' for the external ID increment; existing build is unverified.

items.topic: Closed deals reactivated, same record reused
items.statement: The current approach discussed with the client: a Closed deal can be reactivated, and if the same partner combination resumes later, the same deal record is reused and keeps receiving signups. Kobi called it the closest they got with the client and named versioning as the alternative if it does not work.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we tried to like uh talk through this with them and the best or the closest we got is um we this is where this close status comes. / Kobi Kunasekaran: if they resume that same deal a year later uh for that exact same partner, exact same combination, they are going to reactivate that deal um and reuse the same deal record um and it's going to keep feeding new signups into that same deal.

items.topic: DRA handling on reactivated closed deals
items.statement: Handling of updated deal rep assignments sent by the CMS when a closed deal is reactivated has not been figured out.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: presumably the CMS is going to send an updated deal assignment like we haven't figured out the handling for that yet

items.topic: Retirement replaces need for deal versioning
items.statement: Kobi had proposed deal versioning to the client as an alternative. In this meeting he concluded the Retired status covers creating a new deal with the same makeup, so versions are needed only if the client needs multiple non-retired deals with the same makeup active at the same time. Cedrick agreed. Client confirmation is still pending (see the separate action to confirm with the client).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: If that doesn't work the alternate solution which which is what I proposed to them is start / Kobi Kunasekaran: versioning the deals. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So actually I think this the retirement status works for both without / Kobi Kunasekaran: necessarily needing another version. I think where a second version comes into play is if they could have the same makeup active sorry multiple deals with the same makeup active at the same time and / Cedrick Infantado: Makes sense.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier proposal to the client: add a deal version number as the alternate solution; now retirement is the preferred path.

items.topic: Document retirement as the versioning answer
items.statement: Kobi will update the documents after the call to say explicitly that retirement handles same-makeup new deals and versions are only for simultaneous active duplicates.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I need to make sure to remember this after the call because I'm going to update the documents to say that explicitly. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we only introduce versions if they need multiple deals with the same makeup active at the same time.

items.topic: Commercial terms as dated child object
items.statement: Commercial terms will become a dated child object to track changes, with no overlapping dates. Whether commercial terms are required before activation is still to be decided.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we're going to turn this into a child object that is dated so we are able to track those changes. … Um and then there'll be on whether this is required before activation or not. … there should be no overlaps in the dates

items.topic: Other deal fields that change over time
items.statement: Other deal attributes, such as redeposit requirements, may change over the deal life cycle; this was not discussed with the client. Such cases may need a new deal with the same makeup.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: there are other things like redeposits for example we didn't talk about if this is going to change over the life cycle of the deal and it could right / Kobi Kunasekaran: if if they that that happens again then I think those are the uh cases for requiring a net new deal uh with the same makeup but perhaps with like a version number or like an effective date or something like that to differentiate them.

items.topic: Confirm changeable deal fields and versioning with client
items.statement: Kobi will raise it with the client again: confirm commercial terms points, whether anything else on the deal could change and need tracking, and whether adding a version makes sense.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we we'll bring it up to them again because even for commercial terms, I need to confirm some things. … I'll make sure to confirm if there's anything else that could change on the deal that we might need to keep track of on a daily basis. Uh, and whether it just makes sense for us to add a version.

items.topic: Activated deal cannot return to New
items.statement: Once activated, a deal cannot go back to New by any user method; each other status has its own defined path.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: once the deal is activated it can't go back to new right uh by no user user method um all the other statuses are going to have a specific uh workflow or path

items.topic: Retired is terminal; Closed can reactivate
items.statement: Retired is the only status that fully locks a deal; nothing is editable after retirement. Closed means the deal is not actively pursued but can be reactivated later.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the retired status is the only one that completely locks a deal. So once a deal is retired, nothing should be editable because presumably it's been replaced by something else. … closed means it's they're actively not pursuing that deal, but it could become reactivated later

items.topic: CMS-side handling of synced statuses
items.statement: What the CMS does with each synced status needs to be coordinated with the client.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: What they do with these statuses, I think that's like we need to kind of coordinate with them.

items.topic: Affiliate link changes trigger CMS resync
items.statement: Besides status changes, adding, removing or changing the status of affiliate links must flag the deal for a CMS resync every time.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: there's also affiliate links if they add remove changes status on affiliate links that needs to uh indicate somewhere that the deal needs to be synced so um those two things will trigger a reync every single time

items.topic: Sync trigger mechanism on the deal
items.statement: The mechanism to request a sync is not decided; Kobi thought a checkbox or date on the deal, to be confirmed in the user stories.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't know the exact mechanism on how we allow the system to trigger a sync. I I'm thinking it's just going to be like a check uh check box or like a date or something on the deal. like we'll confirm in the user stories.

items.topic: Save CMS response on deal; error email
items.statement: When a sync runs, the CMS response is saved to a field on the deal. On errors, an email notification with the initial payload and the response is sent for troubleshooting. Kobi restated the notification email at the end.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: when a sync is requested, we're we're going to build the uh payload, send it to the CMS, and capture the response and save it to the respective field on the deal so we know what happened with it. Um, if there are any errors, um, I wanted email notification with the initial payload and the response so we can troubleshoot easily. / Kobi Kunasekaran: notification email that has the thing because we can use that for troubleshooting purposes.

items.topic: Store result only, not payload, on deal
items.statement: Kobi first said payload information would also be stored on the deal, then corrected himself: only the result/response is captured on the deal, not the payload.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we store those those payload information on the deal record as well so that we can use that for troubleshooting / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah, actually, no. I don't think we capture the payload. Just a result. Um, and the result should be like whatever response it is. that comes back.
items.supersedes_hint: Reversed within the same discussion: payload storage on the deal dropped; result only.

items.topic: DRA push from CMS is Phase 2
items.statement: Phase 2 of the CMS integration: the CMS will send deal rep associations (rep, deal, effective from/to, assignment status) back to Salesforce after managers assign links to reps. It is not scoped yet and needs client input; DRA work starts after Phase 1 is live and tested.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: that deal affiliate link rep association gets pushed back into Salesforce so that's going to be phase two of the CMS integration um that we still need to spec account and get input from them. / Kobi Kunasekaran: once that's live and we're able to create the deals and links here and test that out, um we will need to start picking up the DRA uh DRA design.

items.topic: Staging object for inbound DRA calls
items.statement: Kobi is leaning toward a staging object that captures raw DRA API calls and a Salesforce process that maps external IDs (rep, deal, affiliate link) to create DRA records, instead of direct upserts. He plans to propose to the client what their system should send. Final call deferred to Phase 2.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: whether we just let them upsert directly in the DR DRA record or we handle it the way we do with SLC's where we have the staging object to capture the raw uh raw API calls … I'm leaning towards the second one / Kobi Kunasekaran: but we'll have to kind of sort that out in phase two. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think I'm just going to like propose them what we need for VRA uh what their system should send and then we'll set up like a staging object to capture the raw requests and process it.

items.topic: Diagram the DRA flow once mapped
items.statement: Kobi will add a diagram for the DRA (Phase 2) flow once it is mapped out.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm going to add like a additional diagram once we map it out.

items.topic: Phase 1 sends deals and links; group tickets
items.statement: For this phase the CMS integration strictly sends deals and affiliate links. The related deal tickets (new statuses, conditions, screen flows) are prerequisites in the same epic and will be done together.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But for CMS integration for this this phase, it's it's strictly we send the deal and affiliate links over um and any of the related deal tickets that we just talked through like the additional status um the conditions, the screen flows, I think those are all kind of part of the same epic, right? … So, go group it all together. We'll get it all done um at the same time.

items.topic: Link DRAs to affiliate links?
items.statement: Whether DRAs link to specific affiliate links: ideally yes, but historically one link was shared by several reps; in a recent call the client said it is now one link per person. They will try to capture the link in the DRA and decide at DRA scoping. Kobi said the linkage should be informational and not block processes.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So that's a great question. Um ideally yes. Um the only concern is that it might not be onetoone. … I think in one of the recent calls they said that they're not doing that anymore that it's just one link per person. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, when we scope out the DRA, uh, design, uh, we'll make sure to include it and then we can make a decision on whether it's going to be linked or not at that point. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Technically that linkage should be more in likeformational and not like I don't think it should block any processes at this point.

items.topic: Add link ID to SLC/signups for reporting
items.statement: The SLC does not send the link today. Kobi suggested adding the link ID (not the URL) so signups can be tied to a specific affiliate link and reported by link.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: even for the SLC though today I don't think they're sending the the link uh right now / Kobi Kunasekaran: so we should add the link ID or something like that here too so we're able to link the signups to the specific affiliate affiliate link too. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And not not URL but the link ID

items.topic: Link code is required, not unique
items.statement: Cedrick said the link code field is only required, not unique.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct. Yeah. and link codes. It's supposed to be unique, right? That's how we set it up. / Cedrick Infantado: No, it's only required.

items.topic: Link external ID = link code + deal ID
items.statement: Add a link external ID to the JSON payload and requirements if not already there: link code plus deal ID as the unique identifier. Like the deal external ID, once set it cannot change even if the link code changes; changing it needs an intentional admin task that clears it so a new one is generated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: yes let's if we don't already have a link external ID in the JSON payload and the requirements let's add a link external ID and do the exact logic that we just talked about which is going to be the link code plus the deal and that becomes the unique identifier. … once it's set it can't be changed even if they change the link code
items.asr_note: 'electional ID' = external ID; 'link optional ID' = link external ID [ASR?]

items.topic: Scope and add link external ID
items.statement: Kobi will scope the link external ID and add it after the call.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I'll I will scope that and add that in once I go through this call later.

items.topic: Retry rules by CMS response type
items.statement: Business rejections and 400 (payload) errors do not auto-retry; timeout, network and other reason codes auto-retry.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, business rejection, no automatic loop, 400. I think 400 means something's wrong with the payload. / Kobi Kunasekaran: so no retry but timeout network any of the other reason codes uh automatic retry

items.topic: Progressive retry window then notify
items.statement: Kobi suggested a progressive retry window (a couple of minutes, then 10 minutes, then an hour), up to three or four retries, then notify someone for a manual retry. He was not sure how this works with flows.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't know how it works with flows uh versus others but I think like in the past what we've done is like you know retry uh a couple minutes later if that fails retry 10 minutes later if that fails uh retry an hour later and up to like three or for retries before it gives up. Uh and once it gives up, it notifies somebody so that we can uh we're able to do a retry manually.

items.topic: Manual retry checkbox, single and bulk
items.statement: Ops/management need a way to retry a sync without a status change, usually a checkbox, which also supports bulk retry. The automation entry criteria are a status change or this checkbox being true.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: there should be a story somewhere here that that also gives us ops slashmanagement a way to retry without status changes. So usually that's like a checkbox. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So it gives us both the individual record level retry and bulk level. … it's going to be one of the entry criteria, right? Status change or this checkbox is true.

items.topic: Add retry checkbox story if missing
items.statement: Kobi will add the manual/bulk retry story if it is not already defined in the user stories.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: If it's not defined in these unit stories, uh I'll make sure to add that in

items.topic: Unknown payload limits may force Apex
items.statement: The API spec accepts up to about 200 deals per call but gives no limit on affiliate links per deal or total JSON characters. Payload size could decide Flow versus Apex.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the API spec, I think it says like it can accept up to like 200 deals per call, but it doesn't say if there was any limits to the number of affiliate links per deals or like the total number of characters that we can send in the JSON payload. / Kobi Kunasekaran: keep that in mind in terms of like how much how many characters we can store for like uh an API call because that might change flow versus

items.topic: Check Airtable for max links per deal
items.statement: Kobi will try to find the upper limit of affiliate links per deal from the current Airtable data.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So I'm going to try to see if we can find that out from the air table uh data that we have right now.

items.topic: Verify Flow nested-array limit
items.statement: Cedrick thinks Flow has a limit of about 13 nested arrays within an object but is not sure and needs to check.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: How many? I think it's I'm not sure. I have to check. Uh on top of my mind, I'm thinking uh I think it's 13 nested um arrays within an object. So I I need to try that.

items.topic: Send full link list; absence = CMS removal
items.statement: Current design: every sync sends the entire affiliate link list; a link deleted in Salesforce is simply absent from the payload, which implies it should be removed in the CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: but for the time being we assume that we send the entire link payload. we never delete a link. If we delete a link, um the payload will just not have that link in the payload and that implies that the link is no longer uh sorry that implies that the link should be removed in the CMS.

items.topic: Future card: skip synced closed links
items.statement: Link lists grow as deals cycle between closed and active, making payload size unpredictable. A possible future ticket would stop syncing affiliate links already sent in a closed status; the CMS would then need to stop treating absence as deletion. Kobi will take it as a future enhancement card; no change to current design.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: maybe this warrants another bure ticket to not sync an affiliate link once it's already been sent to the CMS in a closed status … But we also need to make sure that they interpret that same behavior uh and don't assume that if a affiliate link is no longer in the payload that is deleted / Kobi Kunasekaran: So for current design, I don't think it should matter but uh I'm I will take this away as a card for uh future enhancement.

items.topic: Store sync errors on deal, not new object
items.statement: Sync errors are stored on the deal object (in a separate sync tab), not in a new error object. A sync error does not change deal status (sync status decoupled), a retry clears the error fields, and field history tracks failures. Cedrick agreed given the timeline.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think for simplicity, let's create it in the deals object. … we're not going to change the status. So we're decoupling the deal status from sync status. / Kobi Kunasekaran: so I propose that we track field history as much as possible. / Cedrick Infantado: Yeah given the time constraint I don't think so that we can accommodate error
items.asr_note: 'CRM sync tab' (line 655) likely = CMS sync tab [ASR?]

items.topic: Dedicated error object deferred to later phase
items.statement: A separate error object is pushed to a possible later phase if it becomes a problem; Cedrick said it is not doable for the October 9 target because it would also need client input.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then we can scope out a error object in later phases if it becomes a problem. / Cedrick Infantado: but still we have to communicate it back to the client and then take their opinion or suggestion on that / Cedrick Infantado: So if we're targeting October 9, so that's not doable, I think.

items.topic: Working target date October 9
items.statement: Cedrick referred to an October 9 target when assessing the error object; the transcript does not say what exactly is due on October 9.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: So if we're targeting October 9, so that's not doable, I think.

items.topic: Reports on outstanding failed syncs
items.statement: Kobi will build reports, which can be subscribed to, that show deals that have not synced.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I can I can build some reports. we can subscribe to. They'll be able to see uh any outstanding deals that haven't synced yet.
items.critic_note: Gemini Details says Kobi 'committed to building reports and subscription dashboards'; transcript says 'I can I can build some reports. we can subscribe to' and does not mention dashboards. Added to gemini_disagreements.

items.topic: Flow vs Apex left to Cedrick
items.statement: Kobi left the Flow versus Apex choice to Cedrick, based mainly on payload size and whether batching works.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then flow versus Apex. I'm going to leave this up to you. … if that's going to be a problem then it might make sense to work uh go with Apex.

items.topic: Add New and Retired status values
items.statement: The existing statuses are fine except that New and Retired must be added as statuses, with user stories.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The only thing is the new and retired need to be added as new statuses. Um there should be us stories for that.

items.topic: Push user stories to Jira tonight
items.statement: Kobi will review the stories and push them to Jira tonight so Cedrick can pick them up tomorrow; some will amend existing tickets. Kobi will message Cedrick when they are pushed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm just going to go through them, make sure these are still like accurate that there's nothing else to amend and then I'll have these pushed over by tonight. You can pick them up tomorrow. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'll send you a message as soon as these are all pushed to CMS. Sorry, not CMS to uh Jira

items.topic: Build order: prerequisites, CMS, then UI
items.statement: Cedrick will start with the prerequisites (field creation and tracking) tomorrow, then the integration. Kobi agreed: prerequisite deal updates first, then the CMS integration, then UI components; screen flows and guided paths can come later but must be ready before the client tests.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: maybe I'll start with those uh by tomorrow first and then I'll proceed with the um with the integration itself. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I think that makes sense. … we just need to make sure that the screen flows and the guided paths are ready before they're able to test. So I would prioritize it as like anything that's prerequisite first and then CMS integration.

items.topic: Validations deferred until UI build
items.statement: Validations are deferred to the UI work unless one blocks the automations; big stories go first so validations do not get in the way of testing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: validations and stuff also TBD I think like I'm thinking when we do the UI we'll add a validation but if there are anything that is like blocking for the automations that's when we might have to consider something / Cedrick Infantado: Let's go uh first with the big with the big stories first / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah agreed

items.topic: Confluence first, then Jira is source
items.statement: Kobi works in the Confluence page first, creates Jira tickets and adds the Jira links back to Confluence; once a ticket is in Jira, the Jira ticket is kept updated so there are not two sources.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: as I create the Jira ticket, I'll add the Jira link in here. Um, and then once it's in Jira, we we just keep the JR ticket updated. Um, so we don't need to like we're not looking at two different sources. / Cedrick Infantado: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

items.topic: Cedrick saw a minor UI issue
items.statement: When asked about other WagerTech topics, Cedrick said he had seen a minor UI issue earlier but did not think it was worth the meeting time. It was not described or assigned.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: I've seen something uh earlier but um it is just a minor UA issue but yeah I don't I don't think it's worth our time right

items.topic: Confluence design docs still incomplete
items.statement: Kobi said he had not reviewed every part of the AI-generated design. Some stories from the original MD files are not yet in the Confluence page, and the AI tool was still filling in the missing items at the time of the walkthrough.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: just a disclaimer like I haven't gone through every single thing. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So I noticed that there were some stories from the MD file that aren't here.
items.asr_note: track = Claude [ASR?] in 'track works really well with using confluence'

items.topic: Cedrick to connect Confluence knowledge base
items.statement: Kobi told Cedrick to point his AI agents at the Confluence folder and hook up Confluence as a connector, and use it as the running knowledge base for why fields exist; Slack stays available for questions. A Slack-integrated bot is a goal but Kobi has no time for it yet. Cedrick said he will connect it once he works on the CMS integration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, in the meantime, just hook up Confluence as like a connector and uh uh have it processed / Cedrick Infantado: and connect that one once I'm working with the CMS integration or anything on the needles.

items.topic: Post-activation statuses mostly informational in Salesforce
items.statement: Kobi said that, for the most part, setting the post-activation statuses has no further effect on the Salesforce side; they are visual or informational. Inactive is the exception with its signup-based automation. Closed is the ops way to show that no more signups should be sent to the deal.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And what happens when these statuses are set on the Salesforce side? Um, it I I actually defined most of those already. So, um, for the most part, honestly, nothing. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And the it's going to be uh visually or informational.

items.topic: Deal versioning would ripple into client CMS
items.statement: Kobi said adding a deal version would also require the client's CMS and end-user workflows to change, and he thinks the client may not fully see the implications until they use the process. His approach is to build enough now, leave room to expand later as a follow-up, and get feedback from real use first.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But if if we end up adding a version here, then that means their their CMS also needs to be adopted and by extension their user enduser workflows need to be adopted / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we need to get feedback and see how it works in practice before we like change it all from the beginning.

items.topic: Affiliate link handling when a deal closes
items.statement: Kobi assumed that when a deal is closed all its existing affiliate links are deactivated (not deleted) and a new set of links is created on reactivation, which makes the link list grow. This is his assumption and was not confirmed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: presumably I'm assuming all of the existing links will be deactivated uh not deleted but deactivated and then they're going to create a new set of links next time it's activated.

items.topic: Lean Jira stories; design spec in Confluence
items.statement: Jira user stories will state only what to build; the design spec, workflow diagrams and the reasons stay in Confluence, which also serves as internal documentation for later troubleshooting. Cedrick agreed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So trying to separate it where the user story is just like what we need to do. Um but if you need to understand the why and the overarching uh plan and stuff uh check back in confluence for the whole thing. / Cedrick Infantado: Yeah, that makes sense.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Enforced standard 5 makeup fields to define a unique deal structure.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Operator, partner, market country, market state, vertical, and source. I guess it's not five fields, it's more than five, but those are the deal makeup fields for a deal.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary says 5 makeup fields and uses past tense 'Enforced'; transcript lists six fields, says 'it's more than five', and describes design, not something already built.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Introduced a screen flow for deal creation defaulting to a new status. / Triggered an initial CMS sync upon successful deal activation and pre-check validation. / Configured subsequent deal status changes to automatically trigger CMS synchronization payloads.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we are going to do a screen flow um that uh it's mostly packed out um that they're going to use instead to create a new deal.
gemini_disagreements.why: Quick notes use past tense (Introduced, Enforced, Locked, Triggered, Configured) as if built; the transcript is a design walkthrough of planned work.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Kobi Kunasekaran and Cedrick Infantado agreed that commercial terms will be handled as a separate section in the screen flow that users can complete during deal creation or add later (00:16:44).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: there I'm thinking about an additional section for commercial terms uh which is a another design that I'm working on um that I will I still need to finish and add in
gemini_disagreements.why: Cedrick did not speak to this point; Kobi presented it and said the design is unfinished and a bolt-on for later. Agreement is misattributed.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that pre-activation modifications remain flexible, while commercial terms and affiliate links must be addressed prior to activation (00:19:18).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I I want to say that they need to do it before they activate the deal, but that's a EBD to clarify with them.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary hardens an open point. Links-before-activation is TBD with the client; whether commercial terms are required before activation is also open (line 437).

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Kobi Kunasekaran decided to proceed with the staging object approach for phase two after the initial integration phase goes live and is tested (00:52:29).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm leaning towards the second one / Kobi Kunasekaran: but we'll have to kind of sort that out in phase two.
gemini_disagreements.why: Transcript is a leaning/proposal to bring to the client, not a decision.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Cedrick Infantado asked whether affiliate links and deal rep associations are interconnected, and Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed they should be linked (00:53:34).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, when we scope out the DRA, uh, design, uh, we'll make sure to include it and then we can make a decision on whether it's going to be linked or not at that point.
gemini_disagreements.why: Kobi said 'ideally yes' but explicitly deferred the decision on linking to DRA scoping.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Kobi Kunasekaran emphasized that signup records must include a link ID rather than just a URL to ensure accurate reporting by link (00:54:56).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so we should add the link ID or something like that here too so we're able to link the signups to the specific affiliate affiliate link too.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary says 'must'; transcript is a suggestion ('we should add the link ID or something like that') with no confirmation.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Timeout and network errors trigger automatic progressive retries up to 4 attempts.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I don't know how it works with flows uh versus others but I think like in the past what we've done is like you know retry uh a couple minutes later ... and up to like three or for retries before it gives up.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary states a firm 4-attempt rule; transcript is a hedged suggestion of 'three or four' based on past practice.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Flow supports a maximum limit of 13 nested arrays within an object.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Cedrick Infantado: How many? I think it's I'm not sure. I have to check. Uh on top of my mind, I'm thinking uh I think it's 13 nested um arrays within an object. So I I need to try that.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary states an unverified recollection as fact; Cedrick said he was not sure and needed to check.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The team targets October 9 for completing the project launch.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Cedrick Infantado: So if we're targeting October 9, so that's not doable, I think.
gemini_disagreements.why: Transcript only mentions 'targeting October 9' in the error-object context; it does not say this is the project launch.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Kobi Kunasekaran committed to building reports and subscription dashboards to surface outstanding failed deals (01:07:20).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We I can I can build some reports. we can subscribe to. They'll be able to see uh any outstanding deals that haven't synced yet.
gemini_disagreements.why: Transcript mentions reports that can be subscribed to, said as 'I can'; no dashboards are mentioned. Summary adds dashboards and hardens to a commitment.
